utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we'll start with the examination of the next witness, we'll first turn into private session, or closed session I think is what would be appropriate in the present circumstances.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in public session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Ostojic, just for the public I informed the public that when we were in private session you made a solemn declaration that you would speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, could you please state your full name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Velibor Ostojic, born on the 8th of August, 1945.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Ostojic, did you receive a copy of the witness statement which was compiled by the Legal Officer of the Chamber and subsequently translated into Serbo-Croatian and sent to your home address on the 19th of June, 2006?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to read that statement?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have read it. I have read the entire statement in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are there any corrections you would like to make to that statement?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, there are some corrections that are needed in this text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please tell us where we find the --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll try, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you refer to the paragraph first.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 2, item 2. The paragraph entitled "professional career." It says that I worked as a journalist in Radio TV Sarajevo, and it should read that I worked there as a language proofreader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- before we continue, I have the full volume of B/C/S through the English translation. Can perhaps this is the way to -- I hope that it's now adjusted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have the same problem, Your Honour, so it's very difficult --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you speak a few more words, Mr. Ostojic, perhaps repeat what we just said so that we ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Page 2, item 2, paragraph entitled "professional career." In line 1 it says "journalist," whereas it should read "language proofreader."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then in the same paragraph, that is to say the same item, in line 3 it should say "minister of information in the coalition government of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any further corrections?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the same paragraph, the last line that explains the structure of the top staff in the ministry, at the end instead of "deputy secretary," it should just say "secretary of the ministry."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have some difficulties to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's in paragraph 2. It says "vice-secretary was a Croat." The witness, I assume, means the word "vice" should be removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Ostojic, where we read: "The deputy was a Muslim and the vice-secretary was a Croat," that you would like --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Deputy -- no, no. It should say "that ministry was headed by a Serb, the deputy was a Muslim, and the secretary of the ministry was a Croat."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So "vice-secretary" is now replaced by "secretary of the ministry." Yes, any further --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Item 3 on the same page, that is to say the next one. Instead of what it says here that the Council of Ministers was an idea just on paper, it should say that the Council of Ministers was a decision of the Assembly of the Serb Deputies that was supposed to be prepared by Mr. Simovic, deputy Prime Minister for state administration in the coalition government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that the words "an idea on paper prepared" are now replaced with "a decision of the Serb deputies that was supposed to be prepared," and then we continue with "By Mr. Miodrag Simovic, the deputy Prime Minister for state administration in the coalition government," as is already in the text. Any further correction, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The next sentence in the same paragraph that reads: "The Council of Ministers did not function as a body," it should read as follows: "The Council of Ministers had not been established and did not function as a body."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we insert the words "had not been" ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could the witness please be advised not to speak at the same time when the Judge is speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The words "had not been established and" are inserted here. Mr. Ostojic, any other correction?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 5 on the same page. The sentence that starts with the following words: "After the Dayton Agreement and after the first parliamentary elections, I was a deputy in the Chamber of Representatives." What is missing is: "Of the parliamentary Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we add after the "House of Representatives of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Any further corrections, Mr. Ostojic? May I ask you whether we have a similar amount of corrections during the whole of the document? Because that would take us hours and hours here in court, and we might try to find another solution then for that. Do you have a similar number of corrections on later pages as well, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, there are changes on the next pages, too, even more than until now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber invites the parties also to see how we could practically resolve this because under normal circumstances you would invite the witness to put them down on paper and have them worked in, but since we are relying on translations provided by The Hague and not by Belgrade, there might be a problem in doing it in any different way. At the same time, to spend here the whole day in court all of us correcting which seems to be not major changes -- Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: One suggestion, Your Honour, would be to take a break and have Mr. Ostojic make his corrections with the assistance of a language assistant in Belgrade, fax those to us immediately as to be distributed to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It could even done perhaps in his B/C/S version of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It could be, and if that could be distributed then we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then that it would be translated here. At the same time, of course, we are not having the guidance of the -- what will be the final statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I, broadly speaking, endorse that, but could I urge the Court to tread very cautiously when the Chamber suggests that these may be "not major changes." The first page is unlikely to be major, but we don't know what is to follow thereafter when we get to the substance of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course there are two matters. I thought they were not major changes, and let's also not forget that this is a statement based on an interview of which we have little transcript. So therefore, we know what exactly was said during the interview. Let's try to ... Mr. Sabbah, could I address you for a second? Mr. Sabbah, could you have a -- do you have the B/C/S copy of the statement of Mr. Ostojic there?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it be possible and do you have the facilities to make all the corrections Mr. Ostojic thinks he has to make on paper and then send them by Telefax to The Hague? Do you have facilities to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would just ask the question whether you would like it also to be translated into English or just the B/C/S statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you -- well, if you would have facilities to have it translated into English, but are the translators sufficiently qualified to do that job? Otherwise, it should be done in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If you give me one moment, Your Honour, I can certainly find out and report back to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then -- I suggest that we'll have a break, that during this break you find out whether you have the facilities needed to do it. If not, please report this to The Hague and we'll then resume. If you have the facilities, I would expect you to assist Mr. Ostojic in making all the corrections. I also add to that, Mr. Ostojic -- yes, that we do not expect you to redraft the whole of your statement, of course, but to make all corrections which are needed for us to properly understand your statement and you may keep in the back of your mind that the Chamber and the parties have the advantage of having had the possibility to read the transcript of what you literally said during your interview. We'll then adjourn without --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We're a little concerned about what Your Honour has just said to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could Your Honour make sure the witness understands what Your Honour is saying and is of a like view, because perhaps if he could in his language explain to you what he now feels he needs to do, we might know where we're going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, could you please -- this is a request by Mr. Josse, Defence counsel, could you tell us whether you understood and how you understood what you're invited to do at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I intervened in the text. It seemed to me that when the transcript was being written out some of my words were omitted, and therefore certain thoughts had not been completed and may therefore get a completely different meaning. My interventions do not actually amend the text or change the statement. The changes are there only to complete each and every thought so that it would be complete, accurate, and comprehensive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, at least most important, Mr. Josse, and I think that's well understood by the witness is that this statement reflects exactly what he thinks he said and what, at least, he takes responsibility for at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Particularly the latter, I would suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I added that not without reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Another way of dealing with it would be - and I am just asking the parties whether that would be an acceptable way of - is just go paragraph by paragraph, ask Mr. Ostojic to add or to correct whatever he wants without writing it all down at this moment. And then finally have in evidence the statement as amended in the transcript of this hearing, which doesn't make it --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's acceptable to the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We have no observations on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I just receive some additional information which might help us out even further, that is that I do understand that Mr. Ostojic has prepared all these corrections in writing already on the document; therefore, I now suggest to the parties that we'll ask Mr. Ostojic to read out slowly whatever corrections he has made and that he'll then sign the corrected statement, that it will be sent to The Hague by Telefax anyhow, and that a translation will then be further prepared here of the statement as a whole. Mr. Ostojic, since you -- I do understand that you have made these corrections already all in writing, perhaps we could continue if you slowly read them so that we have them in our transcript. Then later the text will be sent to The Hague for final translation. I think you were at the end of the fifth paragraph. Is that the only correction you would like to make in paragraph 5, adding "of Bosnia-Herzegovina"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we have again a problem. Could you please repeat your answer. So my question was: Was there anything else in paragraph 5 apart from adding "of Bosnia-Herzegovina," what you would like to add or correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please slowly read what you would like to --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 5, paragraph 5, the last sentence in it, instead of "by which my political career was ended," I think I said "by which my political activity was ended." And this is what it should read there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We move on. Anything more in paragraph 5?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph 6?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 6, in the last line, "again I was not a member," the word that is missing is "of a single Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further corrections in 6?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the following page at the beginning of the paragraph it says: "The legal provision put a ban on simultaneously holding a political and executive position." What is missing is: "The legal provision on the role of MPs."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please always very precisely point at -- are we still in paragraph 6 or are we in another paragraph at this moment?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 6, page 3, the first line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. One second.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: After the words "a legal provision ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said: "On the role of MPs" should be --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What is missing is: "The law -- the legal provision of the law on the election of MPs and deputies."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any further correction in ...

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In the following line, at the end of the thought where it says that "people were elected as members of the Crisis Staff through their political positions," I believe that it should read: "Members of Crisis Staff through local bodies," instead of "political positions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's corrected in "local bodies," instead of "political positions." Anything else in paragraph 6?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph 7, yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 6 there is nothing else. Paragraph 7, the third line from the bottom of that paragraph, i.e., the seventh line of paragraph 7. Instead of "business" it should state "inner."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please read again the line so that we -- because I do not find the word "business" right away. Could you read the whole of the line so that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please read the whole sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the whole sentence, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The sentence begins at the end of the sixth line of paragraph 7 where it says: "It was not in the core office of the Prime Minister but in the expanded office." It should be: "It was not in the inner office of the Prime Minister but in the expanded office of the Prime Minister."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It now has been -- "core" has been replaced by "inner." Anything else in paragraph 7?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The second sentence in it. Instead of "the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska did not deal with foreign media activities," it should read: "The Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska did not deal with foreign media."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The word "activities" to be removed. Yes, anything else?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Instead of "foreign media activities," it should read "foreign media."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the word "activities" is moved out --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I would like to add to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 7 at the end of the thought: "However, it helped the journalists representing foreign media."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would like to add this to paragraph 7. Is that correct? Or at the end of --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps that was a mistranslation. "However, it helped the journalists representing foreign media." Yes, Mr. Ostojic, anything else in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, nothing. Page 4, paragraph 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The last thought in that paragraph which reads: "Volunteers and students of foreign languages worked there," and it should read: "Students, volunteers of foreign languages, worked there," instead of "volunteers," as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say the word "students, who were the volunteers." "Students, volunteers of foreign languages ..."

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else in paragraph 12?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, nothing in paragraph 12. And nothing until paragraph 17 on page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What would you like to correct in paragraph 17?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 17, there is a substantive error here at the end of that thought. It reads: "I did not attend any meetings with Mr. Krajisnik other than the Assembly sessions where Mr. Krajisnik was present." No, that he chaired because he was the chairman. He was the president of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It now reads: "Other than the Assembly sessions which Mr. Krajisnik chaired." Anything else in paragraph 17?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There is nothing. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And next correction would then be in what paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I believe I said at the beginning of that paragraph: "I'm not sure that the Supreme Defence Council existed in 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then read that --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "I'm not sure whether a Supreme Defence Council existed in 1992."

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that is my only correction there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So -- but if you say then following: "But I did not attend any session of the Supreme Defence Council nor did I attend any" -- well, if you do not know whether it existed, should we then also read --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I really am not sure whether it existed or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. "I'm not sure whether Defence Council existed in 1992" --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I did not attend any of its sessions. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. To be understood whether there were any or not is another matter. And then the last that you did not attend any session of the Presidency remains as well?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Next correction, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The next correction is in paragraph 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "I could have consulted with Mr. Krajisnik ..." "I may have consulted with Mr. Krajisnik in his capacity as president of the Assembly about draft laws." And what is missing here: "Or with his associates."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it then reads: "I could have consulted with Mr. Krajisnik or his associates"?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct. "Or with his associates."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that this should read: "I may have consulted with Mr. Krajisnik."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "I may have consulted with Mr. Krajisnik or with his associates."

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 20, line 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In my translation there is a mistake which is more down to the style. "The Presidency of the Assembly had its own information service," and I believe it should read: "The Presidency of the Assembly had its own information service."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter notes that the mistake is in the gender that was used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that doesn't change anything in the English. Next correction, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The next correction is on page 6, paragraph 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Line 5. I believe that the translation into my language is not logical; therefore, I would kindly like this to be corrected. Instead of: "The media did not favour any parties that might have supported an ethnic group," it should read: "The media were not equally in favour of the parties."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It now reads: "The media were not equally in favour of any parties that supported ethnic groups." Please, next one --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "Which supported national or ethnic groups."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else on page -- in paragraph 22?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next correction. What paragraph, please?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The next correction is in paragraph 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 6. I believe that something was omitted from the translation, and this is a thought in which I said that: "When it came to the division and separation of channels, this was something that was discussed by all the parties and coalitions, and this was not only the position of the Serbian side." And I would like this sentence to be added to the end of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to find it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At the end of paragraph 23. This is not there; it is missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it's not there. Please read slowly what is missing exactly.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This is something that should be added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "The division of channels was something that all the parties in the coalition discussed publicly."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "And this was not the position of the Serbian side only."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Next correction, please? Paragraph number?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 6, there are no more corrections there. However, on page 7 in paragraph 24 in the second and third lines there are some illogical parts; therefore, I would suggest that this thought which reads: "Radio Banja Luka, Glas Srpksi and Radio Bijelina became important media at the regional level even before 1992" instead of "during 1992." In other words, "Radio Banja Luka, Glas Srpski and Radio Bijeljina became important media at the regional level before 1992." This is what the sentence should read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's been corrected. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 25, I believe that I explained at the time that not only journalists, refugees worked in the local media, but also the journalists who were otherwise employed there. What is missing here is that "the local media were under the control of their founders, which was the local community." I would like this to be added. And it says here: "The programme or editorial policy was decided by journalists who were refugees and who had left the RTVSA, or who had previously worked in the local media." This is what I would like to see added to that sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is added.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "And whose founders were local communities." This would be all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 27.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Line 1 and line 2, there are mistakes in the names of the transmitters. That is why I would like to make a distinction. In the first line it should read: "As to the alleged take-over of the transmitters on Mount Kozara, Mount Pljesevica, Ciganiste, Majevica, and Trovrh." This is wrong. It should read: "As to the alleged take-over of the transmitters on Mount Kozara and Ciganiste," and that is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we leave out Pljesevica, Majevica?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pljesevica, Majevica, and Trovrh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All three are taken out.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My explanation should be added: "Pljesevica is the territory of Croatia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll come back later to that, what you would know about the three transmitters that have been taken out now. Please, your next correction would be in paragraph ...

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My next correction is in paragraph 29 on page 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I remember that there was a question during the interview about re-routing of the transmitters and -- or redirection of the transmitters, and I said that this was a reaction of the individuals on the ground who were not satisfied with the way RTVSA reported, because it was not objected. And I would like to add this thought at the end of that paragraph. "This was a reaction of some individuals on the ground."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "Who were not satisfied with the reporting of the RTVSA."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your next correction would be in paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The next correction, paragraph 34, page 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When we spoke about Radio Petrovac, the case of Radio Petrovac that is, I believe that I said in addition to the thought at the end of the paragraph: "Moreover, Radio Petrovac had an insignificant broadcasting range," but I also added that this was a minor case that I was not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we add there: "But this was" --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "This was a minor case that I was not familiar with."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 35, page 9. In answering the question whether the media and the editorial policy of Republika Srpska had any information or propaganda plan, I referred to the archive of the media Republika Srpska that is in place and that was at the end of the final thought in that paragraph. But this is lacking here. It is not there. That is why I suggest: "There was no editorial policy in the media of Republika Srpska that might have inspired or influenced some individual crimes, and there was also an information or propaganda plan which can be ascertained by the inspection of the main media of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, next correction.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Second line from the end of that paragraph, i.e., the penultimate line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Instead of: "This alleged statement is a projected statement," I referred to the well-known thesis from psychology which reads -- it should read: "This alleged statement is a projected thought."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. "Statement" being replaced by "thought."

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Instead of: "A projected statement," nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the next correction would be?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 10, paragraph 38. I believe that during the interview I mentioned a public session of the coalition government, the session that took place in 1991 at which the decentralisation of the local government in Bosnia and Herzegovina had been discussed. Your Honours, I would like this to be added to the end of the paragraph: "The decentralisation was publicly discussed by the coalition government of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991." This is what I would like to add to the -- to this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It has been added. Next correction or addition, please.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Paragraph 39.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: A substantive mistake. Here in the penultimate line it says in my copy: "According to page 2," and I believe that it should read: "According to item 2."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Page" is replaced by "item." Next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Paragraph 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With regard to the meeting, during the interview I expressed my doubt that any such meeting had ever been held. And I don't see it in my translation. Therefore, I would like this to be added to the paragraph in the following form: "I doubt that any such meeting ever took place."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be after the sentence where you said: "I absolutely deny the allegation that I chaired such a meeting with Mr. Karadzic and General Mladic." And then you would like to have added there: "I doubt that any such meeting every took place." Yes, please, next one.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct. Thank you, Your Honour. Next correction is in paragraph 41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In the second sentence, a part of my thought is missing. It says here: "It was not within the purview of the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska to follow the events at the local level and the activities of the military structures." "It was not within the purview of the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska to follow the developments at the local level and the activities of the military structures -- local military structures."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we add: "The activity of the local military structures." Yes. Next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Within the same paragraph in line 8 there are mistakes in the translation, therefore I would like this sentence to be corrected to read better. "I do also remember that General Mladic and I both attended a meeting in the beginning of May 1992 which was a rather general meeting." And the explanation in the next sentence is that: "This meeting took place after the Assembly session on 12 May 1992." What is missing here is: "In Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You changed, apart from adding the place, in English it did read: "This meeting could have taken place after the Assembly session." And the end of the sentence is: "But I may be misremembering." Would you -- I now do understand you said "the meeting took place," instead of "could have taken place."

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I haven't got it here in the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at the end it says: "But I may be misremembering." Is your statement now that the meeting took place or that the meeting may have taken place or could have taken place?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I still claim that it is possible that it may have been held -- oh, I found it. I found it. "Possibly I do not remember all details correctly," as I stated. And what I stated is that "in actual fact that meeting was held by other officials of Republika Srpska," which is not contained in this text. And that is why I said that this was a general meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what you now add as a matter of fact is that it was -- that the meeting could have taken place after the Assembly session on the 12th of May, 1992, in Banja Luka, and that you may not remember all details. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then your next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph number?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 44, the first sentence. It reads as follows: "I do not recall whether the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska issued accreditations to journalists who visited camps and detainees." But the rest of the thought is missing. "However, it did issue permits to all journalists who came to Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "However, it did issue permits to all journalists" --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "All journalists who came to Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "And it took care of them." And in relation to that, I unequivocally stated the following fact. That: "In the territory of Republika Srpska at that time, not a single journalist was a casualty."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The last correction is on page 13, paragraph 48.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, paragraph 48 deals with your personal health situation. If there's anything you would rather tell us in private session, for reasons of privacy, please tell us. But what would you like to change? But please address me if you'd like to do it in private session.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There is no need, Your Honour. I can say it right here that what is missing is that I am a heart patient and that I have stomach ailments, which is not a secret. And the latest findings have supported this, and I confirmed that to you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, we have added your heart condition and stomach ailments and the latest filings supporting this. Mr. Ostojic, have you made all your corrections?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I then -- do you want to add or are these corrections -- anything you would like to add, is that already included?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I made the corrections by remembering what I said in the interview. It's not that I'm changing the text, so I really don't have anything else to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then could I invite you to sign your statement, unless you have done so already, and perhaps to initial each page of it.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have already signed the statement and initialled all the pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then please give it to the local -- yes, the local representative of the Registry. Mr. Registrar - and now I'm addressing Mr. Registrar in The Hague - the statement would need an exhibit number and that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: C6, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: C6. Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I suggest that before the break - we had a late start - I would read the summary of the witness statement -- no, I'd rather do that after the break so that we can see whether any of the changes would need our summary to be -- to be adapted in any way. Yes. Is there any objection against admission into evidence of the corrected statement under Rule 89(F)?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the statement of Mr. Ostojic is admitted into evidence and we'll, only after the break, see whether the summary needs to be corrected as well. Mr. Ostojic, you'll receive a copy of this statement and the parties will also receive a copy of the statement, and a copy of the statement will be -- of the final statement as amended by you will be given by the Chamber. We'll have a break now until a quarter past 11.00. We'll then start putting -- first of all, we'll start reading the -- reading the summary so that the public knows also what your statement is. If it would take more time to check whether any further corrections are needed, the Chamber might decide to postpone the reading out of the summary under Rule 89(F). We'll resume in half an hour from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, I see that the videolink with Belgrade is functioning. Before we put any additional questions to you, Mr. Ostojic, I'll first read a summary of your statement that's to inform the public what we are talking about. You were minister of information in the coalition government of Bosnia and Herzegovina until the 12th of May, 1992, when you became minister of information of Republika Srpska. You remained in this position in the government of Republika Srpska until the end of 1992. As to the Bosnian Serb Council of Ministers that allegedly existed in the beginning of 1992, you stated that it was not established and did not function as a body. You described the tasks of the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska as exclusively related to the legal, technical, technological, and financial side of information. You stated that the ministry had no influence on the editorial policy of the media. You stated that the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska could not receive international or foreign media reports or broadcasts or press clippings of international press organisations, because it did not have the technical resources for that. You stated that the Ministry of Information issued accreditations to foreign journalists. Later on, Radio Television Sarajevo, RTVSA, and Srpska Radio Television, SRT, were responsible for issuing the accreditations. As minister of information of Republika Srpska, you reported to the government and through the government to the Assembly in relation to regulations concerning media and information. You stated that the relationship between you and Mr. Krajisnik was very official and that you did not attend any meetings with Mr. Krajisnik other than Assembly sessions which were chaired by him. You stated that the Presidency of the Assembly had its own information service and that it maintained contact with the media through this information service, not through the Ministry of Information, because it was not within the purview of the Ministry of Information to provide an information service to other governmental organs. You stated that the Main Staff also had its own information service that worked independently. You stated that the SDS did not control any media in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1991. You further stated that, after the failed attempt to amend the law on information in mid-1991, Radio Television Sarajevo came under Muslim control through informal means and secret dealings. You explained that Srpska Radio Television was established in May 1992. The Serbian News Agency was also set up in May 1992. You did not prepare any programming guidelines for these newly established Serbian media. You stated that the editorial policy was decided by journalists themselves who had left Radio Television Sarajevo. Moreover, you stated that there was no editorial policy in the media of Republika Srpska that might have inspired or influenced crimes, that such policy did not exist and that there was no such information or propaganda plan either. You denied the allegation that you said in a radio broadcast in Foca on the 9th of April, 1992, I quote: "Shoot at everything that moves. Slaughter everything that comes into your hands." You stated that this was not your rhetoric and not your style. As to the alleged take-over of the transmitters between August 1991 and March 1992 by Serb paramilitary forces, you stated that this was done by individual groups who were dissatisfied with the editorial policy of Radio Television Sarajevo. You did not remember an attack launched against the Radio Television Sarajevo building in the weeks after Mr. Kalinic had threatened in the session of the Assembly on the 12th of May, 1992 to "destroy with rockets" the Radio Television Sarajevo buildings and the antennae. You also disagreed with the allegations put to you that the SDS party in the end of 1991 and throughout 1992 increasingly came to control the media outlets in the territory of Republika Srpska. You also disagreed with the allegation that the purpose of this was to block, suppress, and marginalise information and opinion that dissented from the SDS policy. This evidence is incorrect, in your view, because throughout 1991 none of the media had new editors, but rather the same editors who had been appointed during communist rule. Only the newspaper Javnost, which was set up in 1991, published political views of the SDS. You considered the claim that the newspaper Glas and Radio Banja Luka were, and I quote, "put under the direct authority of Republika Srpska" to be too strong in its wording because there was no Banja Luka television in 1991. Banja Luka was just a technical centre of the Sarajevo studio of Radio Television Sarajevo. You were told that the Court received evidence that the ministry provided direct assistance to adapt local newspapers "for operation under wartime conditions." You explained that the phrase: "Adaptation of media to wartime conditions" means that the media can technically provide information at the local level. It also means, in your view, that only correct information will be broadcast, because misinformation in times of war may create panic. You stated that the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska could not monitor the media outlets in order to avoid misinformation, because it was understaffed. You moreover stated that the Ministry of Information was not entitled to monitor the media outlets. There was no central body that monitored media outlets, in your opinion. You stated that you did not know about a plan of the Bosnian Serb leadership dating from late 1991 to take over power in the municipalities at the time, but that you later learned about such a plan through the media after the Dayton Agreement. You stated that you did not know anything about the origin or distribution of a document of 19 December 1991 entitled: "Instructions for the Organisation and Activity of the Organs of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina in Extraordinary Circumstances." You did not recall an alleged attack on the village Glogova on the 9th of May, 1992. You stated that you were not present at an alleged meeting in Pale of SDS Crisis Staffs and municipality presidents around the 10th of May, 1992, and you denied the allegation that you chaired such a meeting with Mr. Karadzic and General Mladic and even expressed doubt that such a meeting even took place. You remembered that you and General Mladic attended a meeting in the beginning of May 1992. You stated that you never paid any visits to municipalities with General Mladic. You could not recall whether the government formed teams of ministers for on-site investigations in the municipalities on 24th May 1992, and you could not recall that you were sent on such a mission. You stated that you never visited detention camps. You explained that the Ministry of Information held a record of all accreditations issued to journalists who wanted to visit detention camps. You stated that, on the 26th of July, 1992, you, your driver, and a journalist were ambushed and attacked by the paramilitary group Yellow Wasps and their leader nicknamed Zuco, at a place called Grbavci on the Bijeljina-Pale road. You filed a report with the Ministry of Police. You believe that the police took immediate action to eliminate the paramilitary group after that. And this concludes my summary of your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, I would have a few questions for you. May I first of all draw your attention to paragraph 7 of your witness statement. You stated that the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska had a sector of domestic information, finance sector, a legal service, a technical service, and a press centre. Could you tell us how many persons were employed in the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska in 1992.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What I stated here was based on the law on the ministries in the government which provides for the duties of the Ministry of Information. And the Ministry of Information had certain planned activities and services. However, some of those services, which can be seen from the archive of the work of the ministry, had either one person or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, I'm going to stop you. I'd like you to carefully listen to my question and start first of all to answer my question. My question simply was: How many people were employed in the Ministry of Information of the Republika Srpska in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I believe that at the beginning there were about 12 members of staff and that by the end of 1992, by the end of my term of office in the ministry, there could have been no more than 15 members of staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could I ask you whether they were equally divided over the different sections you described or whether the division was not equal. First, perhaps, domestic information.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In the sector of domestic information, as far as I can remember after such a long time, I had an assistant and two associates whose task was to provide for the needs of domestic media in respect of the work of the Ministry of Information. In the other sectors, the situation differed. The most numerous staff was in the press centre which employed students, volunteers, who were in charge of organising press conferences and of being a contact service for all the journalists and media who visited the Republika Srpska and the Ministry of Information. In the legal service, literally, there was only one person employed and he had a legal background. And the situation was the same in the technical service, where we had, as far as I can remember, a university drop-out and an engineer in electrotechnics. In the finance sector I had only a treasurer. In other words, I did not have either staff or professional capabilities to develop the services as they should have been developed, but they were there in a rudimentary form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, when you said 1992 approximately 12 people employed and by the end of that year not more than 15, did you include volunteers, as you just said, student volunteers, did you include them in those numbers?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They -- they received certain compensation for the work that they did and I have included them as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'd like to move to another subject. May I take you to paragraph 3 of your statement. In your statement, as you amended it this morning, you said that the Council of Ministers was a decision of the Serb deputies that was supposed to be prepared by Mr. Miodrag Simovic, the deputy Prime Minister for statement administration in the coalition government. And you said: "The Council of Ministers had not been established and did not function as a body." I'd like to take you to the minutes of the second meeting of the Ministerial Council of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this is found under the first tab. Could the document which is P65, tab 82.1, in the bundle be shown to the witness. That is the second meeting of the Ministerial Council of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina held on the 17th of January, 1992. Have you got that in front of you, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There should be a B/C/S version as well for you.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I've got it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ostojic, according to these minutes you were appointed president of the Commission of Public Services. Moreover, according to the same minutes, you informed the Ministerial Council of the activities and the tasks in the field of information and dissemination, according to this document, and Mr. Krajisnik proposed a debate on the relation between the Ministerial Council and the Assemblies. You said that the Council of Ministers had not been established and did not function as a body. The minutes suggest a different situation. Could you please comment on your statement that the Council of Ministers was not established and did not function as a body, despite these minutes?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: First of all, I am totally unaware that there were some activities involving the Ministerial Council -- actually, I'd forgotten about that. In other words, I did not remember any activities involving the Ministerial Council. Second of all, in my view, these minutes reflect an administrative activity with regard to the preparations for the establishment of the Ministerial Council of the Assembly of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And third of all, I did not do anything at all with regard to that position nor can I remember ever having been involved in any activities that would have to do with this position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said that in your view "these minutes reflect an administrative activity with regard to the preparations for the establishment of the Ministerial Council of the Assembly of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." This sounds as if the meeting was focussing on the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina administrative matters. If --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you repeat anything, unless it would have been mistranslated, I see reference made very often to institutions of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina and not just of institutions Bosnia and Herzegovina. Could you please comment on that?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this Ministerial Council should have taken off the ground in order to articulate the political and ethnic rights of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Therefore, it did not touch upon the authorities of the institutions of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That is why I believe -- actually, these minutes reminded me of something that I have completely forgotten. I believe that these minutes reflect an administrative activity by the people who were tasked by the Serbian Assembly of the Republic of -- Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us what role Mr. Krajisnik played in this meeting.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In light of the fact that I have completely forgotten this activity, I can say even less about the activities of these people who are mentioned here. And save for a statement that the most responsible people from the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina attended this meeting, bearing in mind that what I am saying here should be the truth, I cannot say anything more about this. I just can't remember. I believe that -- that all those who were present were present in order to observe the work in this administrative sphere of a body that should have been established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, your statement that the Ministerial Council did not function -- was not established and did not function as a body, is that still your evidence at this moment?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I must be honest and say that the minutes challenge that; however, my recollection of the period have made me state that this council did not function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In my view, it was just an activity that was being conducted and that developed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- but perhaps I first explain perhaps to you a sound that might be very unfamiliar to me -- to you, very familiar to me. In the Netherlands at 12.00 on the first Monday of the month, they usually test the sirens for urgency situations. So if you heard a lot of sirens in the background, that is just a testing exercise and nothing else at this moment. You might wonder what comes to your ears at this moment. Mr. Ostojic, if you say: Well, my recollection was a bit different from what you read here in these minutes, in your recollection then what body, if not the Ministerial Council, performed governmental or executive tasks and functioned as a de facto government of the Serbian people in the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, irrespective of the fact that there is a document describing an activity, I still claim that during this period of time, which is the beginning of 1992, in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina there was not in the sphere of the Serbian representatives a single body that might have had any power, any executive power. All the representatives of the Serbian people in the coalition government worked exclusively in the organs of the executive power within that coalition government. I can claim this because I myself was a participant in the coalition government of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I move to another subject at this moment, Mr. Ostojic. You stated in paragraph 39 of -- yes, but before I move to another subject, Judge Hanoteau has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to stop because no English interpretation is received in Sarajevo. Another way of -- I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Or here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or here. I don't know how much time it would take to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order not to lose more time, Judge Hanoteau will put the question in English so that we can continue, and during the next break have an opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: At least I will try to do it in English. In paragraph 5, at the end of the document, quite at the end, we can read: "A statement about this meeting of the Ministerial Council will be made by Velibor Ostojic." Do you remember to have established such a statement? Do you remember you have accepted to make such a statement and have you made it? I can read: "A statement about this meeting of the Ministerial Council will be made by Velibor Ostojic." Can you read this, Mr. Ostojic? It's --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I cannot find it. I cannot find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On page 6 of the B/C/S version, the last lines above the names -- it reads: "5. A statement about this meeting of the Ministerial Council will be made by Velibor Ostojic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember having accepted --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: -- that mission, and do you remember you have written such a statement?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, I do not remember having written such a statement. Quite simply, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll then, Mr. Ostojic, move to our next subject. In paragraph 39 of your statement you stated that you do not know anything about the origin or the distribution of the document entitled: "Instructions for the Organisation and Activity of the Organs of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina in Extraordinary Circumstances" dated the 19th of December, 1991. Would you please have a look at this document again. You find it as the next one in the bundle which is in front of you. And for the parties, it's P43.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have had a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since you were shown this document by a Legal Officer in Belgrade during the interview, have you been able to recall anything more about this document?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I've looked at this document. Today, like then, I do not recall anything in relation to this document because at that time I was not an official of the Serb Democratic Party, which I stated in paragraph 6 on page 2 of my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because in July 1991 there were party elections within the Serb Democratic Party, and I was not a candidate in that election because that was prohibited by the law on the election of deputies, members of parliament, and state officials in government. That is the reason, therefore, why I did not --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There was a break in the soundtrack, interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I was very busy with my work in the Ministry of Information of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, may I ask you to look at the next document in the bundle, which is a newspaper article from the 12th of March, 1992, Slobodna Bosna, which is entitled: "Serbs, Get Ready for War." You found that, the title?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I will quote some of this article. It starts with the following sentence: "Slobodna Bosna is the only one to publish the 'instructions on the organisation and activities of organs serving the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in extraordinary circumstances' which," but still a quote from Slobodna Bosna, "which the SDS forwarded to the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina through its municipal councils." That is P405 in this bundle. Isn't it correct, Mr. Ostojic, that the newspaper article is referring to the 19th of December instructions; namely, the document you were shown before?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In my assessment, on the basis of many years of work in the sphere of information, I believe that Slobodna Bosna is alluding first and foremost to the Assembly of the Serb People in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Council of Ministers that was -- well, it's supposed to be made complete and start functioning. I could not read the text now. I just glanced at it. I've just seen what is written in italics and I've seen the headlines. So speaking in an ad hoc manner as I look at the text, I see that this is what is being alluded to. Maybe I'm not right. However, likewise what is alluded to in the text and what is suggested by the text is an introduction of a state of emergency in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and only one party is being blamed for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But isn't it true that -- let me move to my next question. What could you tell us about the Slobodna Bosna newspaper, and what coverage did the newspaper have in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, Slobodna Bosna, like another newspaper that appeared at the time in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that was called Vox, were extremist newspapers from the tabloid sphere. What they preferred in this context was that everything they published did not have to be correct necessarily, but it was necessary in order to sell more copies. Therefore, they carried articles of a sensationalist nature, caused turbulence in the public scene, and all of this with a view to selling more copies and have a larger circulation. Slobodna Bosna, from a newspaper that started out as a tabloid with a circulation of a couple of hundred copies, came to a circulation of tens of thousands of copies. The same happened with the Vox newspaper. At the time, when I was minister of information in the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, this newspaper in the ministry itself and in serious journalistic circles was treated as a sensationalist newspaper of extremist journalism and a newspaper that aspired to shape a public opinion that would lead to disagreement, suspicions, conflicts, and of course it was a newspaper that aspired to shape public opinion based on sensations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us approximately in March 1992 what would have been the -- at that moment the number of copies that was distributed of each of these newspapers? You said it started with a couple of hundred, and then -- at this time in 1992, March 1992, could you tell us what approximately the number of copies was?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you permit me, I will try to draw out of my subconsciousness some recollections. The letterhead of Slobodna Bosna said about 20.000 copies. [French on English channel]. Circulation then Vox. In that month --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have again a technical problem. I receive both English and French at this moment on channel 4. Let's continue and see whether we get exclusively English again. Yes, I apologise for interrupting you, Mr. Ostojic. You said 20.000 copies. Could you tell us anything about the --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- distribution geographically.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course. Well, the newspaper Slobodna Bosna was primarily focussed on the city of Sarajevo and other centres in Central Bosnia, Zenica, Tuzla, Mostar, and that's where most of its readers were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Not in Northern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, certainly some copies arrived there as well. I really cannot rule out any areas in terms of this newspaper not having been distributed there. It was sold through the Oslobodjenje retail network, so it could be found at all the newsstands, where you could also find Oslobodjenje, the then-leading newspaper of the republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, do you remember this newspaper article that you saw it at the time or heard about it at the time it was published?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do not dare say anything, that I remember this properly. But what I do remember is that as minister of information I got this paper every week and I wish to state quite openly that in view of the regard I held it in and as a person who was well-versed in the sphere of information, I knew that this was a newspaper that should simply not be believed at all and no time should be wasted on reading that paper. It is quite possible that for weeks on end I did not open that newspaper. Quite simply, I had better things to do and more serious things to do that came from the sectors from the home public and the foreign public, what serious newspapers worldwide wrote about. So I gave more thought to that rather than a paper that, according to my criteria, was a sensationalist newspaper and one that I did not pay any attention to. The reason why I cannot unequivocally remember the headline is the fact that I had a completely negative view, not only of this newspaper but of all the newspapers that appeared then as tabloids, and one knows full well how they increase their circulation, through the method of sensationalism.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, in your statement you said that you learned about this, such a plan after the Dayton Agreement. Could you tell us what exactly you did learn about such a plan after the Dayton Agreement?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I learned of that paper -- or rather, I had occasion to hear at the time about that document which was simply made public. That is what I meant when I said that I heard about this paper after the Dayton Agreement. Because at that time, in view of the activities of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, this document was already being mentioned as something that had appeared during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of the foreign media you just referred to ever published this document or about this document? Did you come across any such information when you read the other media?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I did not find that in the foreign media -- or rather, in clippings, press clippings of foreign media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who selected and who prepared these press clippings?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The sector for the foreign public in the Ministry of Information. There was an assistant minister for foreign media who had a discretionary right to produce press clippings as to what the foreign press wrote every day about Bosnia-Herzegovina. I, as minister, would receive a final version of the text, both from the assistant minister for foreign media and from the assistant minister for the home media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you said that you never came across this document in the foreign media, would that be true for when it supposedly was drafted or -- that is, in December 1991? Was it then that you didn't come across it, or would that be true also for the time when Slobodna Bosna published it in March 1992?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, independently of what Slobodna Bosna wrote, I'm referring to the time when I was minister of information, and that is the end of 1991. I cannot recall that in a press clipping I read this and that the assistant minister for the foreign media submitted such writings to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at a later stage, in 1992, when you were not a minister of the federal government anymore?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then it was particularly the case, in view of what happened in the aftermath. I did not remember having encountered any writings that had to do with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you're telling --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because in the beginning -- I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- you now refer to the time when you were minister of information in the coalition government, but what about the time when you were a minister of information in the government of Republika Srpska, that is -- well, let's say, from the 12th of May, as you told us, until the 20th of December, 1992, did you ever come across in any foreign media any publication about this document?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No. I cannot recall. If I cannot remember something and if I cannot establish something, since I am under oath, I quite simply dare not make any statements that would not be in line with the oath taken. So at the time when I was minister in the government of Republika Srpska, minister of information, this document was not something that I was informed about and it most certainly was not the result of any activity through the Ministry of Information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when you were a minister in the Republika Srpska government, was the -- was the system, as you just described, in the other government, that you would be -- that you would receive clippings of foreign media, was that the same or was it different or ...

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There were some differences. Since the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska had just been established, it did not have financial, technical, or staffing possibilities to develop its activity, as I could have developed activities in the Ministry of Information of Bosnia-Herzegovina because there was no comparison between the conditions, technical, financial, and other, between these two cases of course to the detriment of Republika Srpska. So, for example, the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska did not even try to produce daily press clippings, as was the case during my time at the Ministry of Information of Bosnia-Herzegovina; the conditions I had there could not be compared to the other conditions. Press clippings were distributed every day to all officials of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Presidency, members of the Assembly, members of government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us absent anything about the frequency of, if any, press clippings being distributed when you were in the Republika Srpska government and whether that remained the same in the whole of 1992 when you were a minister or whether there were any changes in it.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: While I was the minister of information of Bosnia-Herzegovina, these clippings were a daily occurrence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For the previous day. The following morning, all the relevant officials and factors in Bosnia-Herzegovina received such reports, and this was something that was done continuously. It was not of a very high quality because sometimes it was done in a haste in order to meet the deadlines. And the technical service with the government had to make the sufficient number of copies for every member of the government and the Assembly. But this functioned on a regular basis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic, my question was focussing on the time when you were a minister of information in the Republika Srpska government. Could you give us information about that period of time.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apology. I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us already that it was different.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, I just made an error. It was a slip of the tongue. Press clippings in the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska were an occasional activity. It happened every now and then. This was not a regular activity because there were no conditions in place to do that. At the beginning of our work, we were duty-bound by the regulation governing the work of the Ministry of Information. We had to pass all the laws for the Assembly within the deadlines, and this was the primary and basic activity during the first half of 1992 in the Ministry of Information of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us anything -- you said it was occasional. How many times, well, let's say, a month you would receive clippings?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to remember in a responsible way. This could have been once in a month we would do a review of the writings in the newspapers, primarily of the domestic press.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said "primarily of the domestic press." My questions were focussing on the international media. What role did the international media play?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me put it simply. We did not have the technical capabilities, and we did not receive foreign press to read, to peruse, to look at the way those journalists who had visited us and used our services ended up writing about us. At one point I said that we tried to create all the security conditions for the representatives of the foreign media to work in Republika Srpska, and I believe that we were successful in that because we made to provide safety for all the journalists, and every one of them was satisfied with our services.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to move to another subject, Mr. Ostojic. In the 3rd Assembly Session, which was on the 11th of December, 1991, you made the following comment when asked about whether you proposed the establishment of Serb Assemblies in the municipalities. And I'm referring the parties to P65, tab 62. You find the document in the bundle. Mr. Ostojic, it's the next document in the bundle. Could you please look at page 24 of the version in your own language, and it's page 16 in the English. You said: "In places where we can have no political influence on the life and work of the municipalities, in places where our representatives serve only" -- have you found it, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I'll then resume. " ... in places where our representatives serve only to fulfil the formal requirements for the functioning of a government which produces decisions against the interests of the Serbian people, Municipal Assemblies of Serb representatives must be formed. And in places where even this is not enough, municipal territories of the Serb people must be constituted." This ends my quote. Mr. Ostojic, how did you envisage municipal territories to be formed in areas where Serbs were, as I understand from your speech, were in the minority?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I spoke publicly about this issue at the sessions of the coalition government of Bosnia and Herzegovina which raised serious questions about this issue.
