And the topic was the decentralisation of power and expressing needs at the local level of every ethnic group who cannot exercise their political and constitutional rights as a result of being a minority. In this case, and I'm going to read about the last sentence which the interpreter cannot interpret because it was read out too fast, and I primarily mean the legal -- the legal norm, the name of which is a personal autonomy of a minority group in a certain territory. It is possible that I did not use the right terminology, but this is what I meant. And this statement of mine is not a heresies, and I said that also in my statement in one of its paragraphs that at the time a discussion was going on in the government and the republican Assembly about the decentralisation of power and the request of all the three ethnic groups to establish new municipalities and to find a modality by which all the local nationality communities might be satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's still -- you made in this speech -- you make a distinction between the establishment of Assemblies of Serb representatives and where that is not enough, municipality territories of the Serb people must be constituted -- again, my question is, because you didn't fully answer that: How did you envisage municipal -- and that is municipal territories of the Serb people to be constituted in areas where Serbs were in a minority? How would you do that?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, this is an opinion about a discussion, and one cannot be entirely precise, but I'll try and be as precise as possible at the moment. Wherever there is a majority ethnic group, they have to be provided with a legal possibility to establish a new municipality. And the deputies are representatives of the local government, and this is just a symbol that has to represent the elected government in that newly established municipality. And if the same people is a minority in other places, municipal territories of that people have to be established. And in those territories, a certain national minority would exercise their personal protection and their personal rights if in a broader region - and there were such cases - they were threatened by the fact that a different ethnic group was a majority in that territory. In that sense, the constitution or the establishment of the municipal territories of the Serbian people or some other peoples in different areas should have taken place if that people was threatened by majority people, who threatened their right of vote and their rights in that territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it at that time the prevailing opinion in the Bosnian Serb leadership that municipal territories should be formed?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The prevalent opinion was that of the people in -- on the ground, and this was not just the Serbian people. And I will illustrate this by some examples. I remember the session of the government. The opinion was to either establish municipalities or municipal territories with a local micro government. In other words, if the leadership of the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina had an opinion about the establishment of new municipalities, that was in conformity with the concept of the decentralisation, and this did not exist only amongst the Serb population. For example, the Serb population wanted to have the municipality of Ozren between Maglaj and Tuzla. The Muslim population, on the other hand, wanted to have a special municipality, Janja. And the Croatian population at the same time wanted to have a municipality near Jajce which had been the municipality of Dobrotin in the past. Namely, quite a long time before that -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you for a second. You made a distinction between establishing Municipal Assemblies of Serb representatives and the establishment or the constitution of municipal territories of the Serb people. So you make a distinction between the two. My question is focussing on whether the Bosnian Serb leadership, whether it was the prevailing opinion at that time among the Bosnian Serb leadership, that municipal territories should be formed, so not only Assemblies to be established, but also municipal territories to be constituted.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No. In the first case, the establishment of the Assembly of the Serbian deputies, the position of the Serbian leadership was in conformity with the Muslim and the Croatian leaderships' opinion. And in the second and third cases, it was only at the level of discussion as to how to overcome numerous local problems in the functioning of local authorities. And also, with regard to the establishment of these municipal territories of a single people, what was meant was the territories where those peoples did not have a representative in the government, and they were without representation in the government. They did not have any MPs or deputies or members of government in those areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that. But my question is whether it was the prevailing opinion that it would be sufficient to establish Municipal Assemblies of Serb representatives, Assemblies, the plural, or whether the Serbian -- Bosnian Serb leadership also wanted to constitute municipal territories. You make that distinction in your speech.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believed that the difference in the position of the leadership of Serbs did exist. There was a prevalent position that within the decentralisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina there should be a demand for the Municipal Assemblies. And the second issue was just in the realm of discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand that Assemblies should be formed, but whether municipal territories should be constituted was a matter of discussion and not something one had -- they had made their mind on yet. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I used in my question the expression "the Bosnian Serb leadership." How did you understand this expression when you gave your answer?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What I meant was the representatives of the Serbian people who had been elected in the elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 18th of November, 1990, and I meant those at the republican and local levels, and I primarily had in mind the members of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Serbian deputies in the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I had in mind the members of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina from the ranks of the Serbian people and all of us MPs in the municipalities that belonged to the Serbian people and that had been elected in the elections. In other words, the leadership of the Bosnian Serbs is something that I regard as a structure that was elected by the people, starting with the local level to the republican level. I do not mean just the leaders thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And who did you consider to be the leaders of what you now say is a large number of people you call the leadership? Who were the leaders in that leadership then?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I make a distinction here. I said the leadership of the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I mentioned people ranking from the deputies in the local Assemblies to the members of the Presidency. The leadership is the leadership of a political party. In this case, I meant the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You made a distinction. You said: Well, you gave a long list of people you considered to be the Bosnian Serb leadership. And you say: "Something that I regard as a structure that was elected by the people starting with the local level to the republican level. I did not mean just the leaders thereof." Who did you consider to be the leaders thereof?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The leaders are those that were elected by the people in some elections, those who articulate the political will of that people. And this is regardless of who the people are, the Serbs, the Croats, the Jews, because all of them had representatives in the government and in power.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You made a distinction between the leaders of the structure that was elected by the people and that structure as such. I'm now, for the second time or third time even, asking you when you said: "I do not mean just the leaders thereof," and that was in relation to the leaders of that structure of elected -- of persons elected by the people, who did you refer to when you said: "I do not mean just the leaders thereof"?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When I said "the leaders," and I believe that I've already answered that question, I meant those who were in top positions, members of the Presidency, MPs, and members of the Presidency of the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And as opposed to that, political leaders or leader is the president of the political party that articulates that will. In other words, the political leader is the president of the Serbian Democratic Party. And leaders of the Serbs are all those who were elected and who belong to that pyramid from the local level to the republican level. And the higher the point on the pyramid was, the more responsibility that person had for the leading the structures of either local or the republican power.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostojic. We'll have a break. We have, after the break, only half an hour still to go, but we first have a break of 20 minutes. We'll resume at a quarter past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see no videolink yet. Mr. Ostojic, I'd like to move to another subject. In the interview you were asked about the 16th Assembly Session on the 12th of May, 1992, in Banja Luka. You appeared there as a speaker, and you referred to travelling with Mladic on the day before to villages in Herzegovina. You explained in paragraph 41 of your witness statement that you travelled together with Mladic by helicopter to Banja Luka on the 11th of May because the road between Banja Luka and Bijeljina was closed. I'll read out to you what the transcript of this Assembly session says. And for the parties it's P65, tab 127. You find it in the bundle. Page 31, English, page 22 of the B/C/S version. I read the relevant portion to you, Mr. Ostojic. You said: "I have witnessed a confirmation of what Mr. Brdjanin has said about the Muslims and their conduct in relation to Serbian rule, while travelling yesterday with General Mladic and being in contact with Muslims from one village in Herzegovina where you can see precisely who can be -- either the master or the servant, and that nothing can be when they are with us. And we do know what kind of masters they make - then we have genocide - and what kind of servants -- respecting the authority and awaiting what we will feel like saying." What, Mr. Ostojic, was the purpose of this visit to a village in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: First of all, as for this visit to a village in Herzegovina, it is some kind of a mistake because no such visit took place. I don't know. I cannot remember and I don't know that I went out into the field and in what context with General Mladic. This trip from Pale to Banja Luka was a trip taken by MPs and candidates for cabinet members in a helicopter, but we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Ostojic, you said: That trip, I did not travel to a village in Herzegovina. So what I said on the 12th of May what you did on the 11th of May is incorrect. That's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said that in paragraph 41 of my statement on page 11, and I'm perplexed now by some statements of my own and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- these events that I do not seem to be able to link up. Now, what is this all about? I know exactly that on the 11th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no -- well, most important for us is what happened on -- whether or not you travelled with Mr. Mladic on the 11th, and you say you did not. So therefore the question why you travelled with Mr. Mladic, I take it that the answer would be the same -- that that's -- since it is a mistake you could not give us an explanation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I did not travel on the 11th. I travelled towards Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That can be checked in the government documentation, which government members travelled on the 11th of May from Pale to Banja Luka and arrived in the evening of the 11th of May because the Assembly took place on the 12th of May. I don't know where this comes from, these papers saying that I went somewhere else. On the 11th of May I travelled from Pale to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did you ever travel with -- or did you ever go somewhere together with Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I could only have mentioned in this entire account that I heard a discussion or that people were talking about some village in Herzegovina. But on that day, I absolutely claim that I was not in any village in Herzegovina. I absolutely claim that on the 11th of May I travelled from Pale to Banja Luka. That is what I absolutely assert, if anything can have the value of an absolute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move on. In the 16th Session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly, that's still this session the 12th of May, General Mladic stated the following, and it's found in the English version, page 35, and the B/C/S version page 26: "Please," said Mr. Mladic, "please let us not set before ourselves goals that will bring us down. Let us set before ourselves the goals we can achieve. Many of you have helped me. I already said this a few days ago. I keep on repeating certain things. I said this in Nevesinje before the top leadership of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and before an even more select political leadership in Belgrade." Could you tell us, Mr. Ostojic, what gatherings Mr. Mladic was referring to in this portion of his speech?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I listened to the question, I am trying to have a look at the text --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- and what Mr. Mladic stated so that I could answer the question responsibly. As for his encounters with the representatives of the local authorities, if they did take place, Nevesinje included -- well, those are the kind of encounters I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not the kind of -- do you know anything specifically about any meeting or gathering in Nevesinje?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, as for these meetings I found out precisely from this statement that was then made in Banja Luka. As for what was done specifically, I don't know. At any rate, it was my understanding that this was a general type of meeting where he met with the local structures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you present at the meeting where Mr. Mladic -- a meeting that took place in Nevesinje?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I did not attend this kind of a meeting. Simply, I find all of this quite new and unknown to me. There was no need for me to attend such a meeting. There was no context that would make it necessary for me to attend such a meeting. At that time we candidates for cabinet members in Republika Srpska were under the pressures carried out by the legislative branch in order to elect a government of Republika Srpska on the 12th of May in Banja Luka. The basic law on government of Republika Srpska had to be prepared for that purpose, too. And within that basic document, the law on the government, every minister-designate was supposed to prepare the relevant article of that law that pertained to his ministry. I remember that this article that has to do with the field of information, that is to say of this law in Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know whether Mr. Krajisnik was present at the meeting in Nevesinje or a meeting, as just referred to by Mr. Mladic, a meeting with an even more select political leadership in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think that at this meeting in Nevesinje, no one from the Presidency of the Assembly or from amongst the candidates for government members of Republika Srpska were present. None of us were present because we were engaged in this normative activity. I am unaware of this meeting in Belgrade and I cannot state anything in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this Chamber has heard evidence which said that you, Mr. Ostojic, met with General Mladic in Nevesinje before the 12th of May. What do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. Again, I say -- I have to say that all the days in May, after returning from that village where my father was buried, I spent all of these days in my work related to constituting the Ministry of Information. And during those May days, I did not leave Pale at all, which can be checked in the rules of the government of Republika Srpska and my daily engagements. There is documentation related to all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to take you to next subject. The record of a joint meeting of the National Security Council and the government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina held on the 10th of May, 1992 is before this Chamber as evidence. For the parties P64A, tab 617. And you'll find that as the next document in this bundle. Now, at this meeting, an agenda for the upcoming Assembly session on the 12th of May was prepared, and it reads under item number 1(a) as follows: "Report on the political and war situation in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The report will be prepared by the president of the National Security Council." And then it reads: "(Velibor Ostojic has been charged with preparing the report with the assistance of the minister of interior and national defence)." Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, do you remember being charged with the preparation of the report on the political and war situation in the Serb republic?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, without this document, I could not remember. But now I see in the document that this was the duty that I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well that's reading from the document. Do you have any active recollection of being charged with the preparation?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall. Irrespective of the fact that there is a document in existence, I simply cannot recall from my memory what I did in relation to this duty and whether I actually carried it out with the assistance of these two ministers and how this was ultimately done. During those days there were some exceptional activities on the part of future government members with regard to all of this normative activity and the indispensable legislative activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember that session? And if so, do you remember whether Mr. Krajisnik was present at this joint meeting of the National Security Council and the government on that 10th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As for the sessions held up until the 12th of May, this Assembly took place, too, and I'm trying to remember now. I mean, what I'm trying to say is that I do have some memory of the session being held, but I think that Mr. Krajisnik was not present at this session. I cannot recall that he was present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, in this case it has been alleged that Mr. Krajisnik was involved in the preparation of the agenda for the Assembly meeting on the 12th of May, 1992 and that he may have attended this joint meeting.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't know how he could have been involved in the preparation of this session, if you are referring to this session of the 12th of -- of 10th of May. I was not a member of the inner circle of the Prime Minister, but, quite simply, I cannot remember whether Mr. Krajisnik attended the meeting. And what I'm saying is I wish to confirm what I remember. And if I'm not sure, I am afraid that I would make a grave mistake vis-a-vis myself and vis-a-vis the Court. Once again, I repeat that I cannot recall that Mr. Krajisnik attended this meeting of the 12th -- of the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, just to be sure, Mr. Ostojic, if you can't remember or if you don't know something, please tell us without any hesitation that you don't know or you don't remember. My next question is: Why did the National Security Council and the government prepare the agenda for the Assembly session?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Simply put, and with responsibility, Your Honour, I don't know and I cannot remember. But the government was indeed preparing for the Assembly; that I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did that happen at other occasions as well, that is -- that a joint meeting of the National Security Council and the government prepared the agenda for the Assembly in such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No. No. This is an exception as far as I'm concerned. I have just familiarised myself with it, but while I was a government member in 1992, I cannot recall any other such meetings. Even physically, the government, after the 12th of May, was in a different place from Banja Luka. It moved to a hotel in Jahorina, so even physical distances led to the fact that the government worked independently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to move to the next subject. This Court, Mr. Ostojic, has heard evidence about the airport negotiations, which took place in Lukavica in May 1992. The airport was handed over to the United Nations on the 27th or the 28th of June, 1992. Do you know who took part in the negotiations on the Bosnian Serb side in those airport negotiations?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, first and foremost I think that it was the late Nikola Koljevic who took part in these negotiations. I don't know who else took part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you, yourself, involved in these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No. No. I was not because it was not within the domain of my work as a member of the government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It has been alleged in this case that Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Koljevic, and Mr. Mandic were in charge of the airport and that you, Mr. Ostojic, were also involved in the negotiations. Does that change anything in your previous answer?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No. I absolutely claim that I was not involved in these negotiations. I can just recall that Mr. Koljevic was in these negotiations. I don't know about the others. This is a field that was outside the Ministry of Information, so there are no grounds for the Ministry of Information and its representative to be involved in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Krajisnik did attend or did ever join meetings in which these negotiations were held?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I cannot say that I know anything about that. As far as I can remember, Mr. Koljevic was in charge of contacts with international institutions in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Mr. Ostojic, we have to finish for the day. We'd like to see you back, even if it is at a distance, tomorrow morning, 9.00, at the same place where you are at this very moment. And I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony you have given or the testimony you are still about to give in this case. Do you understand those instructions?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is what I'm doing. I respect your position and I will fully respect it with great discipline and responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we will adjourn for the day. We'll resume tomorrow morning, 9.00, Courtroom I, and continue with the videolink with Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of July, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
